evidence.claim: The 2022 Government Work Report set targets of around 5.5 percent GDP growth, over 11 million new urban jobs, stable macroeconomic performance, deeper reform, higher-standard opening up, innovation, and improved wellbeing.
evidence.title: China releases full text of Government Work Report
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Government Work Report set targets of around 5.5 percent GDP growth, over 11 million new urban jobs, stable macroeconomic performance, deeper reform, higher-standard opening up, innovation, and improved wellbeing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government program text is strong for announced intent and policy direction, but weaker on realized effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material. It was delivered by Premier Li Keqiang for the Xi-led State Council, so it reflects top-state economic direction rather than Xi's sole authorship.
contrary_evidence: The report is aspirational and does not itself show implementation.
Actual 2022 growth later landed well below the 5.5 percent target.

evidence.claim: China released 10 new COVID measures to replace oversimplified one-size-fits-all approaches with more science-based and targeted controls, explicitly ordering localities to correct excessive policy steps.
evidence.title: COVID-19 response further optimized with 10 new measures
evidence.excerpt: China released 10 new COVID measures to replace oversimplified one-size-fits-all approaches with more science-based and targeted controls, explicitly ordering localities to correct excessive policy steps.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy announcement with concrete administrative instructions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to the Xi-led party-state because it represents the top-level pivot in pandemic governance, though implementation ran through health and local authorities.
contrary_evidence: The pivot was late and followed major economic and social damage.
The policy change does not erase the earlier costs of strict zero-COVID enforcement.

evidence.claim: China's financial authorities rolled out 16 steps to stabilize real-estate financing, support reasonable mortgage demand, and ensure delivery of pre-sold housing projects.
evidence.title: China unveils financial measures to bolster housing market
evidence.excerpt: China's financial authorities rolled out 16 steps to stabilize real-estate financing, support reasonable mortgage demand, and ensure delivery of pre-sold housing projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy announcement with a clearly specified policy package and purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Xi-era financial and regulatory apparatus rather than Xi alone; it is still direct ruler-period policy evidence.
contrary_evidence: This is damage control after a severe property downturn, not evidence that the underlying crisis was avoided.
The property market still weakened sharply in 2022.

evidence.claim: Xi said China should pursue high-quality development, improve the distribution system, widen high-standard opening-up, strengthen innovation and talent policy, and make progress toward common prosperity.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping's report to the 20th National Congress of the CPC
evidence.excerpt: Xi said China should pursue high-quality development, improve the distribution system, widen high-standard opening-up, strengthen innovation and talent policy, and make progress toward common prosperity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Xi-authored strategic report is strong for stated intent and self-assessed trajectory, though it remains a self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period strategic address delivered Oct. 16, 2022 and published Oct. 25, 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi as party leader and principal speaker.
contrary_evidence: This is a self-report and mixes aspiration with retrospective claims.
Independent macro sources still described serious slowdown, property stress, and policy uncertainty in 2022.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said China's growth was expected to slow to 2.7 percent in 2022 amid pandemic disruptions and real-estate stress, and it called for deeper structural reforms, predictable regulation, better credit access, and more support for youth employment.
evidence.title: China Economic Update - December 2022
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said China's growth was expected to slow to 2.7 percent in 2022 amid pandemic disruptions and real-estate stress, and it called for deeper structural reforms, predictable regulation, better credit access, and more support for youth employment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality independent macro assessment with explicit policy recommendations and date fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is not a Xi-only causal finding, but it is strong independent context for the Xi-era policy environment and the consequences of those choices.
contrary_evidence: It is a forecast and policy recommendation, not a direct ruling on Xi's intent.
Part of the slowdown also came from global shocks and pandemic dynamics.

evidence.claim: IMF staff said China's 2022 growth would be below global growth for the first time in over 40 years, with zero-COVID restrictions, the deep property-sector contraction, and weak global demand weighing on the economy, and it described support for unfinished housing and mortgage relief among the policy responses.
evidence.title: People's Republic of China: 2022 Article IV Consultation
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff said China's 2022 growth would be below global growth for the first time in over 40 years, with zero-COVID restrictions, the deep property-sector contraction, and weak global demand weighing on the economy, and it described support for unfinished housing and mortgage relief among the policy responses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent macro surveillance with clear causation analysis and detailed policy discussion.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2022 IMF surveillance published after the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not direct personal attribution, but it strongly assesses the Xi-led policy regime and its macro consequences.
contrary_evidence: This is staff analysis, not a binding legal finding.
The IMF also recognizes that some support measures were introduced in response.

evidence.claim: The NBS reported 3.0 percent GDP growth in 2022, 5.1 percent fixed-asset investment growth, a 10.0 percent fall in real-estate development investment, 10.5 percent export growth, 2.0 percent CPI inflation, a December youth unemployment rate of 16.7 percent, and rural disposable-income growth faster than urban growth.
evidence.title: National Economy Withstood Pressure and Reached a New Level in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: The NBS reported 3.0 percent GDP growth in 2022, 5.1 percent fixed-asset investment growth, a 10.0 percent fall in real-estate development investment, 10.5 percent export growth, 2.0 percent CPI inflation, a December youth unemployment rate of 16.7 percent, and rural disposable-income growth faster than urban growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary statistical release with full-year outcome data; official statistics still require caution, but this is the core national dataset.
evidence.period_fit: Full-year 2022 outcome release published in January 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These are country outcomes, not automatic Xi credit or blame, but they are the main end-of-year economic results under his rule.
contrary_evidence: Official statistics may understate private-sector weakness.
National averages conceal regional and distributional stress, especially in the property and youth-labor markets.

evidence.claim: The NBS reported that real per-capita disposable income rose 2.9 percent in 2022, rural income grew faster than urban income, and real per-capita consumption fell 0.2 percent, with the median income still below the mean.
evidence.title: Households' Income and Consumption Expenditure in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: The NBS reported that real per-capita disposable income rose 2.9 percent in 2022, rural income grew faster than urban income, and real per-capita consumption fell 0.2 percent, with the median income still below the mean.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary household survey release with detailed distributional measures, though still official data.
evidence.period_fit: Full-year 2022 household outcomes published immediately after year end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level household outcomes are only partially attributable to Xi, but they are the best official evidence of household welfare under his 2022 rule.
contrary_evidence: Urban households' real income growth was only 1.9 percent and real consumption fell.
The release does not isolate ruler-specific causality from pandemic and macro conditions.

evidence.claim: For 2022, China’s UNICEF dashboard shows 98% basic drinking-water access, 96% basic sanitation access, 97% basic handwashing access, and 0% open defecation.
evidence.title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for China
evidence.publication_date: best available: current dashboard with 2022 indicators
evidence.excerpt: For 2022, China’s UNICEF dashboard shows 98% basic drinking-water access, 96% basic sanitation access, 97% basic handwashing access, and 0% open defecation.
evidence.source_locator: environment indicators on the China country dashboard
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN agency data dashboard is strong for country-level service-access context, though it is a dashboard summary rather than a ruler-specific evaluation.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 country indicators shown on the dashboard.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level baseline evidence only; it is not direct proof of Xi’s personal management, but it is relevant welfare context under his rule.
contrary_evidence: This is a national dashboard, not ruler-specific attribution.
The dashboard does not by itself show service quality or political prioritization.

evidence.claim: At the end of 2022, China had 1,345.92 million basic medical-insurance enrollees and coverage remained stable above 95%.
evidence.title: 2022 National Medical Security Development Statistical Bulletin
evidence.excerpt: At the end of 2022, China had 1,345.92 million basic medical-insurance enrollees and coverage remained stable above 95%.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary sector bulletin with explicit enrollment and coverage figures, though still an official report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Xi-era health system and party-state policy apparatus, not Xi alone.
contrary_evidence: Coverage says little about care quality or affordability.
Official reporting may smooth over local access barriers.

evidence.claim: China's basic old-age insurance covered 1.05 billion people at the end of 2022, with 24.3 million more people covered than a year earlier; national unified management of enterprise-employee basic pension funds was launched in January 2022 and 244 billion yuan was reallocated between provinces to support weaker areas.
evidence.title: China continues to expand old-age insurance coverage
evidence.excerpt: China's basic old-age insurance covered 1.05 billion people at the end of 2022, with 24.3 million more people covered than a year earlier; national unified management of enterprise-employee basic pension funds was launched in January 2022 and 244 billion yuan was reallocated between provinces to support weaker areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official summary with clear coverage and redistribution figures, albeit retrospective and self-described.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the end of 2022 and the 2022 reform year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Xi-era national social-security governance rather than Xi personally, but it is still ruler-period institutional evidence.
contrary_evidence: Coverage expansion does not prove adequacy of benefit levels.
The source is an official self-report.

evidence.claim: China launched a private pension plan to complement the existing pension system, with tax incentives and individual pension accounts, as part of a multi-pillar old-age insurance framework.
evidence.title: China rolls out private pension plan
evidence.excerpt: China launched a private pension plan to complement the existing pension system, with tax incentives and individual pension accounts, as part of a multi-pillar old-age insurance framework.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy announcement with concrete institutional design and implementation details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Xi-era State Council policy; it supports assessment of durable social-institution building, though not Xi personally.
contrary_evidence: The plan is optional and market-based, so its reach depends on uptake.
It is a design change, not proof of realized welfare gains in 2022.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Education said 2022 priorities included implementing the 14th Five-Year education plan, strengthening education as a priority in public finance with no less than 4% of GDP, protecting teachers' pay, improving balanced compulsory education, and monitoring implementation.
evidence.title: 2022 education work priorities
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Education said 2022 priorities included implementing the 14th Five-Year education plan, strengthening education as a priority in public finance with no less than 4% of GDP, protecting teachers' pay, improving balanced compulsory education, and monitoring implementation.
evidence.source_locator: sections 5, 6, 15, and 25 of the article text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry policy text with concrete targets and implementation themes, but it is still official self-description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Xi-era education governance rather than Xi alone; useful for assessing service delivery intent and institutional management.
contrary_evidence: An announced priority is not the same as realized access or quality.
Some of the language is aspirational and party-orthodox.

evidence.claim: The Education Ministry said China had achieved county-level basic balanced development of compulsory education across all 2,895 counties, rural schools had improved markedly, and the nine-year compulsory education retention rate had reached 95.4%.
evidence.title: 推动义务教育走向更加优质均衡
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: The Education Ministry said China had achieved county-level basic balanced development of compulsory education across all 2,895 counties, rural schools had improved markedly, and the nine-year compulsory education retention rate had reached 95.4%.
evidence.source_locator: article body discussing the nationwide balanced-development and dropout-clearing achievements
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry article with concrete nationwide attainment figures, though celebratory and not independent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Broad national education-system evidence under Xi-era governance; not exclusive personal attribution, but directly relevant to ruler-period performance.
contrary_evidence: The source is official and promotional.
It does not isolate learning quality or subnational inequality that persists beneath national averages.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that China's strict zero-COVID policy kept residents confined for long periods, impeded access to health care, food, and other necessities, and that an unknown number of people died after being denied medical treatment for non-COVID illnesses.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: China
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that China's strict zero-COVID policy kept residents confined for long periods, impeded access to health care, food, and other necessities, and that an unknown number of people died after being denied medical treatment for non-COVID illnesses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality independent human-rights monitoring with concrete examples and clear period fit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly describes 2022 lockdown practice and its consequences, published immediately after the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The policy was maintained under Xi's leadership, so the harms are materially attributable to Xi-era governance, even if many measures were implemented by local officials.
contrary_evidence: HRW also notes the policy prevented some Covid deaths and illnesses.
The report does not quantify the full national death toll from non-Covid deprivation.

evidence.claim: HRW said people across China peacefully protested draconian Covid-19 restrictions in late 2022, while authorities had repeatedly imposed unpredictable lockdowns on hundreds of millions of people, impeding access to health care, food, and necessities.
evidence.title: China: Unprecedented Nationwide Protests Against Abuses
evidence.excerpt: HRW said people across China peacefully protested draconian Covid-19 restrictions in late 2022, while authorities had repeatedly imposed unpredictable lockdowns on hundreds of millions of people, impeding access to health care, food, and necessities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent NGO release with specific period-linked claims and clear attribution to the central policy environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The nationwide pattern is attributable to Xi-era Covid governance, though this source does not prove Xi personally ordered each local restriction.
contrary_evidence: The protests show civilian pressure and policy responsiveness, not just repression.
This source is partly overlapping with HRW's World Report chapter.

evidence.claim: China announced 10 new Covid measures that told localities to rectify one-size-fits-all excesses, prohibit arbitrary expansion of high-risk areas, reduce mass testing, allow home quarantine for eligible cases, and keep basic medical services and pharmacies functioning.
evidence.title: COVID-19 response further optimized with 10 new measures
evidence.excerpt: China announced 10 new Covid measures that told localities to rectify one-size-fits-all excesses, prohibit arbitrary expansion of high-risk areas, reduce mass testing, allow home quarantine for eligible cases, and keep basic medical services and pharmacies functioning.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy circular with explicit operational corrections and service-protection instructions.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period 2022 policy correction, issued in December 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Xi-era top-level policy reversal through the State Council and joint prevention mechanism; strong ruler-period evidence, but not Xi-alone authorship.
contrary_evidence: The pivot came after major social and economic harm.
Implementation followed severe earlier lockdown damage, so this is corrective evidence rather than proof of earlier restraint.

evidence.claim: The NBS reported 3.0 percent GDP growth in 2022, 5.1 percent growth in fixed-asset investment, a 10.0 percent fall in real-estate development investment, 10.5 percent export growth, and a December youth unemployment rate of 16.7 percent.
evidence.title: National Economy Withstood Pressure and Reached a New Level in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: The NBS reported 3.0 percent GDP growth in 2022, 5.1 percent growth in fixed-asset investment, a 10.0 percent fall in real-estate development investment, 10.5 percent export growth, and a December youth unemployment rate of 16.7 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary statistical release with the standard full-year national outcome series, though official data still deserve caution.
evidence.period_fit: Full-year 2022 outcome release published immediately after year end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country outcomes under Xi-era rule, not automatic personal credit or blame, but the data are the main end-of-year welfare backdrop.
contrary_evidence: Official statistics may understate distress in private firms and local labor markets.
National averages can hide severe household and regional strain.

evidence.claim: The NBS said real per-capita disposable income rose 2.9 percent in 2022, rural income grew faster than urban income, consumption fell 0.2 percent in real terms, and the national median income was 85.1 percent of the average.
evidence.title: Households' Income and Consumption Expenditure in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: The NBS said real per-capita disposable income rose 2.9 percent in 2022, rural income grew faster than urban income, consumption fell 0.2 percent in real terms, and the national median income was 85.1 percent of the average.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary household-survey release with useful distributional detail, though still an official data source.
evidence.period_fit: Full-year 2022 household outcomes published immediately after year end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is country-level welfare outcome evidence under Xi-era rule; attribution is partial but materially relevant.
contrary_evidence: Urban real income growth was much weaker than rural growth.
The release does not isolate the effects of Xi's choices from pandemic and macro shocks.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 evidence of Xi's own assets, liabilities, outside interests, or a personal public correction/admission.
Most of the anti-corruption and data-fraud material is system-level enforcement, not proof of Xi's own candor or self-dealing.
The strongest family-wealth context is pre-2022 and indirect, so its period fit for the target year is weak.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
